risks.risk: Talent availability, retention and competition for specialised skills
risks.note: The MD&A flags talent availability and retention as critical challenges across regions, alongside 'competition for specialised talent' amid an intense hiring market for AI and digital-assurance skills; the company's delivery capacity depends on retaining this talent.

risks.risk: Rapid technological change and intense competition from large IT players, AI-native companies and platform ecosystems
risks.note: The MD&A notes 'the competitive landscape is intense, with large IT players, AI-native companies, and platform-led ecosystems expanding their capabilities,' alongside 'rapid technological change' and 'AI-amplified cybersecurity risks' as challenges that could erode differentiation and pricing.

Regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act (major provisions from August 2026), India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework are tightening transparency, data-lineage and monitoring expectations, described as 'structural shifts rather than short-term compliance exercises,' raising compliance and governance burden for a business serving regulated industries.

The Automotive sector recorded a degrowth due to well-documented global headwinds, showing exposure to end-industry cyclicality; the company's revenue mix is also concentrated toward BFSI, so weakness in any single served industry can weigh on overall growth.

Reported revenue growth includes the impact of currency fluctuations, while growth in constant currency was weaker, reflecting FX sensitivity; the MD&A also cites 'geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainties, and uneven regional performance' and 'supply chain disruptions, energy price volatility, policy uncertainties around tariffs and regulations' as sources of business uncertainty.

risks.risk: Information security, cyber and business-continuity risk
risks.note: The Company's own Enterprise Risk Management framework names 'ISMS' as a distinct risk category covering IT security, cyber risks, information security incidents, data protection and business continuity planning, reflecting the sensitivity of handling client data and systems in a digital assurance business.

The ERM framework separately identifies reputational risk as potential damage to the organisation's brand or image from actions, events or decisions that negatively affect stakeholder perception, which is material given the company's reliance on long-term client trust and repeat engagements.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- AI adoption is moving from pilots to enterprise-scale capability requiring governance, measurable outcomes and responsible oversight, driving demand for digital assurance, data governance and AI validation capabilities
- Regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act (major provisions from August 2026), India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework are structurally raising requirements for transparency, data lineage and ongoing monitoring, increasing relevance of assurance-led services
- Growth in digital payments, open ecosystems, data protection regulation and Global Capability Centre (GCC) expansion in India and APAC is sustaining demand for assurance-led transformation
- Automotive-sector volumes declined due to well-documented global headwinds, causing the Engineering line to degrow while Digitech grew, shifting the revenue mix
- Constant-currency revenue growth was a degrowth of 0.4% (versus 8.1% reported growth), indicating reported growth was aided by currency movements while underlying demand was pressured by the Auto slowdown
- Digital services grew to 50.05% of total revenue from 48.09% the prior year, reflecting a structural shift beyond legacy QA/QE work toward digital engineering
- Competitive intensity from large IT players, AI-native companies and platform-led ecosystems, plus talent competition, is a persistent margin and differentiation pressure that the company addresses via proprietary tools and domain-specific delivery models
- Multi-year, multi-geography engagement with a major global payments technology leader's vendor consolidation initiative, under which Expleo will establish a dedicated digital engineering centre of excellence for core issuing, switching and acquiring platforms
- Phased, multi-year partnership with a leading UAE bank to establish a digital assurance centre of excellence and provide AI Assurance to financial institutions in the region
- 42 new customers added during fiscal 2026, compared with 27 new customers added during fiscal 2025

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Two-pronged approach to talent, regulatory and pricing pressures: embed AI-enabled delivery models leveraging intelligent agents alongside skilled talent, and drive a continuous, organisation-wide AI 360 upskilling initiative
- Continued strategic investment in proprietary AI platforms (Sophia, CodePle, Quasar), responsible AI frameworks and talent upskilling to strengthen positioning as a trusted partner in digital assurance and quality engineering
- Best-shoring delivery model with primary centres in India and supporting offices across the USA, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East to maintain resilience through geographic diversification
- Expand presence in the Middle East (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt) as a strategic growth pillar via digital assurance and AI-assurance centres of excellence
- Pursue large vendor-consolidation and centre-of-excellence engagements with global clients to build lasting operational value and enter new markets
- Continue the shift of revenue mix toward digital services and digital engineering, beyond the traditional QA/QE heritage
- For FY2025-26, the Board has recommended (and the Notice of the 28th AGM proposes shareholders declare) a Final Dividend of Rs. 110 per equity share of face value Rs. 10 each, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM to be held on August 26, 2026.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY2025-26, the Company added Rs. 30.65 Mn to its gross block with capital expenditure, comprising Rs. 8.96 Mn on building & lease, Rs. 10.23 Mn on technology infrastructure, and Rs. 11.46 Mn on physical infrastructure addition. It closed its Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu competence centre (closed February 18, 2026) and consolidated it into the MEPZ branch office in Chennai for operational efficiency, while the Israel branch of Expleo Technologies India Private Limited is in the process of closure. A new wholly owned subsidiary, Expleo Solutions GIFT IFSC Limited, was incorporated in GIFT City, Gujarat, India, on June 14, 2026. The Company continues to operate branch offices in the Philippines, Belgium, Israel and Malaysia, and offices in Pune, Bengaluru and a sales-office-cum-delivery-centre in Mumbai, alongside its five wholly owned international subsidiaries (Singapore, UK, USA, Dubai, Saudi Arabia). moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Over three decades of experience with deep domain expertise across BFSI, automotive, aerospace, retail, manufacturing, energy and healthcare
- Proprietary AI-powered platforms (Sophia, CodePle, Quasar) with an AI assurance framework embedded at the core of every solution
- India's cost-competitive, high-quality talent pool underpinning a best-shoring global delivery model
- Globally recognised quality/security/compliance certifications (ISO 9001, ISO 27001, SSAE 168/ISAE 3402, PCI DSS, AS9100, TISAX) supporting trust with regulated clients
- Long-standing client relationships, including one OEM partnership that crossed the 20-year mark, reflecting high switching costs and reputation
- Attrition rate of 15% for the year, stated as below industry benchmarks, reflecting talent retention as a competitive differentiator

- Talent availability, retention and competition for specialised skills — The MD&A flags talent availability and retention as critical challenges across regions, alongside 'competition for specialised talent' amid an intense hiring market for AI and digital-assurance skills; the company's delivery capacity depends on retaining this talent.
- Rapid technological change and intense competition from large IT players, AI-native companies and platform ecosystems — The MD&A notes 'the competitive landscape is intense, with large IT players, AI-native companies, and platform-led ecosystems expanding their capabilities,' alongside 'rapid technological change' and 'AI-amplified cybersecurity risks' as challenges that could erode differentiation and pricing.
- Evolving AI and data-protection regulation — Regulatory frameworks such as the EU AI Act (major provisions from August 2026), India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework are tightening transparency, data-lineage and monitoring expectations, described as 'structural shifts rather than short-term compliance exercises,' raising compliance and governance burden for a business serving regulated industries.
- Customer-industry concentration and cyclicality — The Automotive sector recorded a degrowth due to well-documented global headwinds, showing exposure to end-industry cyclicality; the company's revenue mix is also concentrated toward BFSI, so weakness in any single served industry can weigh on overall growth.
- Currency and macro/geopolitical volatility — Reported revenue growth includes the impact of currency fluctuations, while growth in constant currency was weaker, reflecting FX sensitivity; the MD&A also cites 'geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainties, and uneven regional performance' and 'supply chain disruptions, energy price volatility, policy uncertainties around tariffs and regulations' as sources of business uncertainty.
- Information security, cyber and business-continuity risk — The Company's own Enterprise Risk Management framework names 'ISMS' as a distinct risk category covering IT security, cyber risks, information security incidents, data protection and business continuity planning, reflecting the sensitivity of handling client data and systems in a digital assurance business.
- Reputational risk — The ERM framework separately identifies reputational risk as potential damage to the organisation's brand or image from actions, events or decisions that negatively affect stakeholder perception, which is material given the company's reliance on long-term client trust and repeat engagements.
